name: Brother
title: Brother Sewing Machines UK: Range, History and Parts
description: Brother sewing machines explained: Japanese roots, domestic, embroidery and industrial ranges, who each suits, and where to find parts and servicing.
intro: One of the broadest ranges in sewing, from simple beginner machines to embroidery machines and industrial equipment.
cardText: Japanese roots, domestic and embroidery ranges, industrial machines.

sections.html: Brother traces its roots to a sewing machine repair business founded in Nagoya, Japan, in 1908. The company grew into a manufacturer of sewing machines and later of printers and many other products.

Brother’s domestic range runs from compact mechanical machines to computerised models with many stitches, automatic needle threaders and one-step buttonholes. They are a common first machine in UK homes.
Brother is well known for embroidery and combination sewing-and-embroidery machines. Check the maximum hoop size and the design file formats each model accepts.
Brother also makes industrial sewing machines used in workrooms and factories, alongside its domestic range.

Brother traces its roots to Nagoya, Japan, in 1908, when it began as a sewing machine repair business. Sewing machines remain one of its core products alongside printers and labelling machines. In the UK, Brother machines are widely sold through high street shops, department stores and independent sewing centres.

sections.h2: Which Brother machine suits which sewer
sections.html:
• Beginners: lightweight mechanical or simple computerised models with an automatic needle threader and a one-step buttonhole are easy to learn on.
  • Dressmakers: computerised models with more stitches, speed control and a range of presser feet.
  • Embroidery: combination sewing and embroidery machines (including the Innov-is range) take a hoop and stitch designs from files.
  • Overlocking: Brother also makes overlockers for neat seams on knits; see our overlocker and embroidery guide.

sections.h2: Common Brother problems and quick fixes
sections.html: Most “faults” on modern domestic machines come down to threading, the wrong needle or lint. Rethread with the presser foot up, fit a fresh needle of the right type for your fabric, and brush out the bobbin area. If the machine shows an error code, the manual lists what it means. See common sewing machine problems.

sections.h2: Parts and servicing for Brother machines
sections.html: Brother machines are among the makes PK Sewing Machines lists on its website. Leicester’s hosiery heritage means the city has deep machinery know-how.

faqs.q: Is Brother a good brand for beginners?
faqs.a: Brother is one of the most common beginner brands in the UK, with many affordable, easy-to-thread models. As with any machine, try it or read the specification before buying.

faqs.q: Can I use generic presser feet on a Brother?
faqs.a: Many Brother domestic machines take standard low-shank snap-on feet, but check your manual for the shank type before buying.
